findings.item: ITEM C — backlog row 22, the stale band register
findings.claim: Row 22 is directionally right (the register IS stale and understates the problem) but WRONG on three specifics: the file, the date, and the count. The band register is NOT in 01_doc_conventions.md and that file has never carried last_updated: 2026-05-27. The register lives at 00_README.md:49-62, which does carry last_updated: 2026-05-27. The 'four of nine' mismatch figure is six of nine as measured. The 40-band has ZERO free slots, not spare capacity.
evidence: 01_doc_conventions.md:1-7 — frontmatter reads 'last_updated: 2026-08-08', NOT 2026-05-27.

git log -p -- 01_doc_conventions.md, filtered to last_updated lines, shows the COMPLETE history of that field: 2026-05-05 (9abff0e) -> 2026-05-21 (9646633) -> 2026-08-08 (5dcd571). The value 2026-05-27 NEVER appears in that file's history. Three commits total.
01_doc_conventions.md:20-22 contains NO band table. It delegates: 'NN is a two-digit numeric prefix from the band table in [00_README.md](00_README.md).'
00_README.md:1-8 — 'last_updated: 2026-05-27'. 00_README.md:49-62 — the actual '## Numbering bands' fenced block. The date in row 22 is correct; it was attached to the wrong filename.

Register band subjects as written at 00_README.md:52-61: 00-09 Meta; 10-19 Ground truth/portfolio architecture/roadmap; 20-29 Agent operating rules/AI-first dev flow/workstation/deploy rules; 30-39 SmartCity OS; 40-49 Design Accelerator + Revit Connector; 50-59 Hauska SDK; 60-69 ECI; 70-79 Bizops + brokerage; 80-89 ADRs; 90-99 Runbooks/postmortems/incident records.

SUBJECT-MATCH measured per directory against the band subject line above: 19_hardware_sovereignty (10-19 = ground truth/architecture/roadmap) NO; 24_adaptive_ui (20-29 = agent operating rules/dev flow/workstation) NO; 64_recursive_loop (60-69 = ECI) NO; 65_sensors (60-69 = ECI) NO; 80_meetings (80-89 = ADRs; holds transcripts/) NO; 90_operations (90-99 = runbooks/postmortems/incidents; holds the two PLANS OF RECORD) NO; 80_adrs YES; 90_runbooks YES; 91_postmortems YES. Mismatched = 6 of 9, matched = 3 of 9.

Directory sanction measured: grep for each directory name across BOTH register files (00_README.md, 01_doc_conventions.md) returns 0 mentions for 19_hardware_sovereignty, 24_adaptive_ui, 64_recursive_loop, 65_sensors, 80_meetings, and 90_operations; and non-zero for 80_adrs (5), 90_runbooks (3), 91_postmortems (2). The only directories the convention set names are at 01_doc_conventions.md:56-61.

Row 22's phrase '90_operations/ ... has no sanction anywhere' is over-broad: it has no sanction in the REGISTER files (0 mentions), but AGENTS.md names it twice as the plan-of-record home, and _catalog/plan_registry.json governs its rows. Correct statement: unsanctioned by the doc-conventions register, load-bearing everywhere else.

40-band occupancy measured slot-by-slot (count of root entries matching NN_* or NN<letter>_*): 40=12, 41=12, 42=3, 43=1, 44=1, 45=1, 46=1, 47=1, 48=3, 49=2. Zero slots in 40-49 return a count of 0. The 40-band is FULL.

Nine bare-number slots carry MULTIPLE distinct documents, violating 01_doc_conventions.md:20-22 ('Use the lowest available number in the appropriate band') and the sub-letter rule at :39-40 ('Don't use sub-letters for independent sibling topics — those get their own numeric slot'): slot 00 (00_README, 00_current_state); 27 (27_MASTER_WDLL_spine_completion_and_depth_engine, 27_engine_evolution_plan); 28 (28_THE_BASTROP_MOLD_engine_build_spec, 28_mcp_first_product_design); 29 (29_mcp_surface_tier_model, 29_scale_warm_architecture); 30 (30_block_cert_harness_spec, 30_smartcity_os); 40 (40_design_accelerator, 40_hauska_map_3d_implementation_brief); 41 (41_host_connectors_program, 41_revit_connector, 41_three_wedge_spine_strategy); 42 (42_design_accelerator_program_plan, 42_stub_thesis_national_twin_substrate); 48 (48_codex_program_plan, 48_cortex_reporting_function_dashboard_spec, 48_cortex_reporting_plan_review_spec). This collision class is NOT in row 22 and is a new finding.

registerClaimsVsDiskSummary.whatTheRegisterClaimsIsFree: NOTHING, explicitly. This is itself the core finding: 00_README.md:49-62 is a BAND table (ten ranges with subjects), not a SLOT register. It never enumerates individual free or used slots. Therefore the row-22 framing 'which slots the register claims are free' has no direct answer — the register makes no per-slot claim at all. The only free-slot signal it emits is INDIRECT and procedural: 01_doc_conventions.md:21-22 instructs 'Use the lowest available number in the appropriate band', which delegates the determination to a filesystem check at authoring time. There is no register-side list to diverge from.
registerClaimsVsDiskSummary.whatIsActuallyOccupiedOnDisk: 72 of 100 slots: 00-31 contiguous except 32, then 33, then 40-65 contiguous except 66-69, then 70-80, 90, 91.
registerClaimsVsDiskSummary.theRealDivergence: Not free-vs-used (the register asserts neither). The divergence is SUBJECT-vs-CONTENT in six of nine numbered directories, plus nine multiply-occupied slots, plus three bands whose declared subject no longer describes their contents at all (40-49 declared 'Design Accelerator + Revit Connector' now holds Cortex/Codex/host-connector/map material; 60-69 declared 'ECI' now holds recursive_loop and sensors; 90-99 declared 'Runbooks, postmortems, incident records' now holds the two plans of record).

findings.proposedDisposition: PROPOSE, do not execute (DEV_PROCESS 5.4 — this is an amendment to canon and an operator ruling): (1) CORRECT backlog row 22 itself — it names the wrong file, and the date it cites belongs to 00_README.md; a reader following row 22 will open 01_doc_conventions.md, find last_updated 2026-08-08 and no band table, and reasonably conclude the row is resolved. (2) Amend the count in row 22 from 'four of nine' to 'six of nine', measured. (3) Grant 90_operations/ an explicit slot and sanction in the register — it holds both plans of record and is named by AGENTS.md while being invisible to the convention set. (4) Re-subject the 40-49, 60-69, and 90-99 band lines to describe what the bands actually hold. (5) Add the nine-slot collision class as a NEW backlog row: it is a distinct defect from register staleness, it violates a rule the conventions state explicitly, and it means 'use the lowest available number' currently returns a slot that is already occupied for anyone authoring in the 40-band. (6) Concur with row 22's 'Renumbering buys nothing' — the 40-band being full at zero free slots means renumbering would cascade, and the sub-letter convention already absorbs growth. Amend the register to match reality rather than moving files.

rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.moment: Writing this close. The contract's minimum close schema is written for a BUILD lane: 'PR numbers + merge SHAs + CI conclusion strings, checkpoint artifact paths'. I am a read-only audit sub-agent. I opened zero PRs, merged nothing, and ran no CI.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: There is no sanctioned way to satisfy a required field that is structurally inapplicable. The three options are all bad: omit the keys (fails a machine check that tests for presence), emit them empty (indistinguishable from a build lane that forgot), or emit prose excuses inside a machine-checkable artifact. The schema also assumes the filer is a LANE, not a sub-agent of a lane — 'lane id' is ambiguous for me (G-09? SA-1? both?).
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Add a required `shape` field to the close schema with an enumerated vocabulary (build | read-only-audit | measurement | dispatch), and make the PR/SHA/CI block conditionally required on shape=build. For non-build shapes require an explicit `notApplicable` array naming each omitted field and why, so omission is a positive declaration rather than a silence — the same principle AGENT_CONTRACT 5 already applies to absences in DATA, applied to the artifact schema itself.

rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.moment: Measuring free vs occupied numeric slots for ITEM C. The rule's incident and its prescribed remedy are entirely about the git four-value case (fs / tracked / untracked / ignored) with the identity fs = tracked + untracked + ignored.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The rule states a general principle ('measure the class you are reporting; never derive it by subtraction') but its only operational content is a git-specific recipe. For a NON-git complement pair — free vs occupied slots over a closed range of 100 — there is no guidance on what the analogue of the four measured values is, or what identity should be asserted. A literal reader could satisfy the letter of the rule with the git recipe and still derive free = 100 - occupied, which is exactly what the rule's spirit forbids.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Generalize 1.3 to: 'when two classes partition a closed universe, measure BOTH with independent positive tests and state the identity that must hold, then check it.' Keep the git four-value recipe as the worked example rather than as the rule body. I applied the generalized form here (per-slot positive test for free, prefix extraction for occupied, identity 72+28=100 checked) but I had to infer that this was intended.

rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.ruleId: AGENT_CONTRACT 5 (empty result / absence) — INTERACTION WITH SCOPE
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.moment: ITEM B. My scope is read-only inside doc_repo. The pull-back loop names a path in ANOTHER repo (mox_demo/docs/adaptive_ui_design_system.md). I cannot test whether that file exists.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The rule says only a positive determination writes an absence, and every absence carries its basis. It is silent on the case where the positive determination is UNOBTAINABLE WITHIN SCOPE — which is structurally different from 'I looked and found nothing' and from 'I haven't looked yet'. The rule gives me no vocabulary to distinguish (a) verified absent, (b) verified present, (c) unobservable from here, and the third is the honest answer for the majority of what row 16 asks. Without that vocabulary the pressure is to collapse (c) into (a), which is precisely the failure the rule exists to prevent.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Add a third state to the absence rule: `unobservable-in-scope`, requiring the agent to name the scope boundary that blocks the determination and WHO or WHAT could make it. I used that shape here by construction, but the rule did not supply it and a less cautious agent would have written 'the loop never fired' as a finding rather than as an unresolved question.

rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.moment: On finding that backlog row 22 names the wrong file and the wrong count, and that row 16 poses a superseded question.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: 5.4 says propose, do not unilaterally remediate — correct, and I followed it. But the backlog is itself the durable artifact 5.3 designates for findings, and it now contains verified-wrong content that will misroute the next reader. Nothing in either file distinguishes a SUBSTANTIVE change (retire a doc, delete a clone — clearly operator-only) from a FACTUAL CORRECTION to a control-plane artifact whose error is proven at source. Under the current wording both require an operator, so a known-wrong pointer stays wrong until the operator gets to it, and every agent that reads row 22 in the interim repeats my work.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Split 5.4 explicitly: structural changes (retirement, deletion, status flips, scope changes) remain operator rulings; FACTUAL CORRECTIONS to catalog/backlog artifacts, where the error is demonstrated at source with file:line, may be applied by the finding agent PROVIDED the correction is logged as a diff in the close and the original text is preserved inline. If that is judged too permissive, then at minimum add a required `knownWrongPending` field to the backlog row format so a wrong row self-advertises while it waits.

rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.ruleId: DEV_PROCESS 3.3 (name what is out of scope)
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.moment: ITEM C asks me to check the 40-band 'AND elsewhere'. 'Elsewhere' is unbounded.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The rule binds the DISPATCHER to name what is out of scope, and my brief largely complied — but 'AND elsewhere' reintroduces exactly the 'unmentioned' failure state the rule names, inside an otherwise well-scoped brief. There is no rule binding the AGENT on what to do when a brief contains an unbounded scope token. I chose to bound it as 'all 100 two-digit slots at repo root, maxdepth 1, files and directories' and to state that bound. Nothing told me to.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Add to section 3: an agent receiving an unbounded scope token ('and elsewhere', 'etc.', 'anything similar') MUST declare the bound it adopted and record the token as a brief defect. Cheap to comply with, and it makes vague briefs visible in closes rather than absorbed silently by whichever agent happened to read them charitably.

rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.ruleId: AGENT_CONTRACT 1 (fan model) vs the dispatch instruction
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.moment: Reading the contract at the start, as instructed, while holding a dispatch that says 'Do NOT spawn sub-agents. You are the deepest worker.'
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The contract's opening operative sentence is 'You are a LANE PLANNER, not a solo executor. You MAY spawn sub-agents,' and it is compiled verbatim into every dispatch INCLUDING dispatches to leaf sub-agents. For SA-1 the entire section is not merely inapplicable but directly contradicted by the dispatch body. It resolved easily here because my dispatch was explicit, but a compiled rulebook whose first section contradicts the mission it is stapled to erodes the authority of the rest — and section 1 also carries the CP1/CP2 checkpoint obligation, which a leaf agent could plausibly read as binding on itself.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Have scripts/dispatch.mjs compile a role-scoped contract: sections 1 and 2 (fan model, interruption recovery) are lane-planner sections and should be omitted or explicitly marked 'not applicable to leaf sub-agents' when the compiled target is a sub-agent. Alternatively add one sentence to section 1: 'If your dispatch names you a leaf worker, this section does not apply to you; sections 3-7 do.'

rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.moment: Reporting 'six of nine numbered directories mismatch their band subject'.
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The rule assumes ratios are COUNTED. This one is JUDGED — whether 65_sensors 'matches' the subject 'ECI' is an interpretation, not a query result, and no counting rule can make it reproducible. The rule is silent on judgment-based ratios, which are common in audit work and are the ones most likely to drift (row 22's own 'four of nine' is the proof: it is the same judgment made differently, with no way to see why).
rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Extend 1.2: a ratio produced by judgment rather than by query must enumerate its members, not just its count, so the judgment is inspectable and re-checkable. I did this (all nine directories listed with their verdicts) but the rule asked only for a counting rule, which for this ratio would have been near-meaningless.

rulebookRulesThatFired.ruleId: DEV_PROCESS 3.2 / AGENT_CONTRACT 5 (verify at source, including your own dispatch's context block)
rulebookRulesThatFired.whatItPrevented: The highest-value rule of this run, and it fired four separate times. My brief told me to verify its own assertion about _projects/ and 24_adaptive_ui both needing an external fact — it was wrong. Applying the same posture unprompted to backlog row 22 caught THREE further errors (wrong file, wrong file for the date, undercounted mismatches) that my brief had presented as settled background. Without this rule I would have opened 01_doc_conventions.md, found no band table, and most likely concluded the backlog row was already resolved — leaving the actual stale register at 00_README.md:49-62 untouched and reporting a clean bill of health.

rulebookRulesThatFired.ruleId: AGENT_CONTRACT 5 / DEV_PROCESS 4.3 (an empty result is not an absence)
rulebookRulesThatFired.whatItPrevented: Prevented the obvious wrong answer on ITEM B. 24_adaptive_ui has one commit, zero since 2026-06-13, and a design_system.md full of placeholders. Every signal available inside doc_repo points at 'dead', and writing that would have been fast and wrong. The rule forced me to ask what positive determination I could actually make — which sent me to repo_intents.md and the 2026-07-02 Chris dispatch, and turned the finding from 'dormant workstream' into 'the loop's source repo was PARKED and its owner's mandate was relocated', a materially different and actionable result. It also forced the same discipline on the 'zero pull-back receipts' count: I read all four grep hits and classified each, rather than reporting an empty grep as proof.

rulebookRulesThatFired.ruleId: DEV_PROCESS 1.3 (measure the class you report; never derive by subtraction)
rulebookRulesThatFired.whatItPrevented: Directly changed my method on ITEM C. My first instinct was to enumerate occupied slots and report the complement as free — one command instead of a hundred. The rule forced an independent per-slot positive test for the free class. That produced the identity check (72 + 28 = 100) which validated both measurements, and the per-slot loop is what surfaced that the 40-band has ZERO free slots — a fact a complement calculation would have reported identically but without the per-slot occupancy counts (40=12, 41=12) that show WHY renumbering is not viable. It also set up the collision finding.

I had verified, source-backed corrections for backlog row 22 (wrong filename, wrong count) and row 16 (superseded question) and could have edited both in seconds — they are factual fixes, not judgment calls, and it would have felt like tidying. The rule stopped it. Worth noting the reason it was RIGHT here beyond obedience: correcting row 22 in place would have destroyed the evidence that the G-09 process test needed, since the wrong row IS the finding. A quiet fix would have left the close saying 'row 22 verified' with nothing to show. Logged as a rule-that-fired AND as tension in the silent/ambiguous list above, because the general case is less clear than this one.

rulebookRulesThatFired.ruleId: DEV_PROCESS 1.2 (every ratio carries its counting rule inline)
rulebookRulesThatFired.whatItPrevented: Forced me to write the counting rule for 'six of nine' before publishing it — which is when I noticed that the number is a JUDGMENT, not a count, and that row 22's 'four of nine' is the same judgment made differently with no visible method. That directly caused me to enumerate all nine directories with individual verdicts rather than publish a bare ratio. Without it I would have shipped 'six of nine' as a correction to 'four of nine' with exactly the same inspectability problem as the figure I was correcting — a drift-for-drift trade.

ITEM A's folder contains 01_local_dev.md with instructions to start two long-running dev servers (pnpm dev on ports 8080 and 19592), and 03_deploy.md with gh workflow run deploy commands. Verifying 'is this project live' by running them would have been a plausible reading of the mission and would have hung the session on a non-exiting process — and the deploy commands would have been outward-facing actions from a read-only audit. The rule made the boundary obvious: every check I ran was a one-shot find, grep, git, or ls.

rulebookRulesThatFired.ruleId: AGENT_CONTRACT 6 / DEV_PROCESS 5.2 (an honest partial close beats a narrated full close)
rulebookRulesThatFired.whatItPrevented: Prevented me from manufacturing a resolution for ITEM B. I could have written a confident disposition ('retire the loop, mox_demo is parked') and it would have read as a complete close. Instead the rule licensed leaving the two-part external fact genuinely open with named answerers and a disposition under each branch. It also stopped me from quietly dropping the parts of the brief's framing that turned out to be wrong — reporting them as wrong is the deliverable.

rulebookRulesThatFired.ruleId: DEV_PROCESS 1.4 / AGENT_CONTRACT 5 (two numbers that should agree and don't = a free finding)
rulebookRulesThatFired.whatItPrevented: Kept me from rounding off the 2026-05-27 discrepancy. Finding last_updated: 2026-08-08 where the backlog said 2026-05-27, the cheap read is 'the row is stale, the file was updated, move on'. Treating the disagreement as a finding instead sent me to git log -p to establish that 2026-05-27 had NEVER been that file's value — which is what located the real register at 00_README.md and made the row actionable rather than dismissible.

rulebookRulesThatFired.ruleId: DEV_PROCESS 6.2 (one authoritative copy; a duplicate is a future contradiction)
rulebookRulesThatFired.whatItPrevented: Shaped the ITEM B disposition. Without it, the natural recommendation on discovering the relocated mandate would be 'repoint the loop at legacy-design-tools' — which would leave doc_repo's 24_adaptive_ui/design_system.md and the @hauska/design-tokens package as two design-system homes. The rule made reconciling them an explicit part of the proposed disposition rather than an omission.

timeToFirstUsefulAction.basis: Counted by hand from my own tool-call sequence. 'Useful action' = the first command whose output became evidence in a finding, as opposed to context loading.
timeToFirstUsefulAction.note: The 4th read (the backlog) was simultaneously the last context read and the first useful action — reading row 16 at :49 immediately falsified the brief's central assertion. So the honest number is 3 pure-context tool calls, ~324 lines of mandated rulebook plus a routing file, before the first evidence-producing read. CLAUDE.md was loaded automatically and is not counted as a read I chose.
timeToFirstUsefulAction.assessment: Low friction relative to the finding rate. The two rulebooks are ~324 lines combined and both earned their read — nine distinct rules from them fired during the work, which is a high hit rate for mandated preamble. The genuine inefficiency is elsewhere: the compiled preamble duplicates content already in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, and AGENT_CONTRACT section 1 was not merely unused but actively contradicted by my dispatch. A role-scoped compile would cut the mandated read for a leaf sub-agent by roughly a quarter with zero loss.
timeToFirstUsefulAction.counterNote: Time-to-first-useful-action is a misleading metric to optimize here and I want that on record. Three of my seven planner-figure findings came from reading the backlog and the register files CAREFULLY rather than quickly. A version of me optimizing this number would have trusted the brief's summary of row 22 and missed all three.

constraintsHonored: READ-ONLY: made no edit to any file except this close artifact. Verified by intent and by tool history — every doc_repo interaction was find, grep, git log/status/ls-files, cat, sed -n, ls, or Read.
Did NOT edit _catalog/repo_cleanup_backlog.md despite holding four verified corrections to it (rows 16 and 22).
Did NOT edit 01_doc_conventions.md or 00_README.md despite the register being demonstrably stale.
Did NOT retire, status-flip, or delete anything. All dispositions are proposals per DEV_PROCESS 5.4.
Did NOT spawn sub-agents (dispatch instruction; I am the deepest worker).

All verification exit-bounded per AGENT_CONTRACT 5: no watch, no tail -f, no dev server, no deploy. Explicitly declined to run the pnpm dev servers in _projects/cortex_workspace_qa/01_local_dev.md and the gh workflow run deploy commands in 03_deploy.md.
Doc_repo commits left to the planner per AGENT_CONTRACT 6: this close is written and UNCOMMITTED.
Every ratio carries its counting rule inline at the point of use (DEV_PROCESS 1.2); judgment-based ratios additionally enumerate their members.
Free and occupied slot classes measured independently with positive tests, identity checked, never derived by subtraction (DEV_PROCESS 1.3).
Unbounded scope token 'AND elsewhere' in ITEM C bounded explicitly to all 100 two-digit slots at repo root maxdepth 1, files and directories; bound declared rather than silently adopted.
Reported planner figures as wrong where measurement showed them wrong (DEV_PROCESS 3.2), including my own brief's framing.
Followed rules I flagged as problematic rather than working around them; every objection is reported, not acted on unilaterally.
